sections.title: New Features
items: UIF Community brings compatibility reports into the app alongside clearly labelled UWUVCI recommendations. Record your own test results and prepare a report for submission.
Shared release history connects the community website and What's New. Preview the changes in a newer version before downloading, with offline history and optional update checks.
UIF Bridge 1.0.6 adds optional per-title digital GamePad button remapping for supported native Wii U software, with saved profiles, discard, and standard-control restore.
Build Projects save reusable .uifproject setups with input verification and relinking. Compare Builds helps identify changes between projects, history, and reports.
Review Wii folder batches with individual titles, artwork, and settings before queueing builds.
Read artwork textures and banner sound from your own Wii disc image, preview supported banners, and capture a frame for your artwork.
Generate title-only menu icons and launch images, with no source artwork image required.
An optional interactive Guide highlights the core build controls. What's New keeps expandable release history available from Utilities.
Source Integrity and local build inspection help check selected files, disc references, and prerequisites before a build.
Advanced cartridge tools apply reusable IPS/BPS patch sequences to a new ROM copy. Wii patch collections provide reviewed executable matches and change previews.
Create and exchange supported digital Wii Remote profiles for compatible firmware rebuilds.
Import owned encrypted local base packages with the matching ticket and your supplied key, or continue using extracted base folders.
Import Existing Data previews supported settings, eligible keys, and extracted bases while preserving the originals.
Reusable manual projects and supported GBA page preparation, personal BIOS-file kits, SD-card checks, and save-backup inventories add more tools around your builds.
Windows x64 and Linux glibc x64 add RVZ/WIA conversion and verification, CHD inspection, and Ogg Vorbis inspection. CHD inspection does not add CHD injection.
Wii U disc tools inspect WUD/WUX images, convert between them, and read title metadata with your supplied disc key.

sections.title: Improvements
items: Compatible UIF Assistant versions use FTP for bulk transfers, with separate HTTP control and verification and a fallback for older compatible receivers.
More reliable pairing and reconnection, remembered pairing where secure storage is available, clearer progress and cancellation, and recorded transfer/install-result recovery.
Assistant 1.0.6 adds supported network, interface, and installation settings with Save, Cancel, and defaults.
The Light theme has stronger button contrast, dark-purple accents, and more consistent text, fields, menus, and dialogs.
Boot sounds support MP3, compatible AIFF, and more WAV formats, with converted-audio preview, the six-second limit, and an optional final fade.
Improved artwork fitting, cropping, templates, and selection previews. Supported PSP sources can supply title and artwork previews.
Eligible Wii Trim builds avoid some large intermediate files, reducing working storage and unnecessary copying.
Clearer readiness links, completed-build actions, background configuration checks, and steady progress while an operation is busy.
Build history retains useful input information after workspace cleanup; saved projects and local builds are easier to review and relink.
Compatibility refresh preserves complete cached results when the network is unavailable and keeps report sources distinct.
Improved NooDS and PPSSPP packaging preserves supplied startup media and prepares missing required startup assets.
Better UIF Bridge connection/status handling and guarded maintenance, plus stronger archive, split-disc, storage, cancellation, and support-diagnostic handling.
Official downloads are available for Assistant, Aroma Bridge, NooDS autoboot, and PPSSPP for Tiramisu.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Complete Wii common-key entries are saved for reuse without requiring a successful build first, including in the RVZ/WIA utility.
Wii Trim retries no longer collide with a temporary ISO left by an earlier attempt.
Mac Save dialogs suggest the correct project and comparison file extensions.
Corrected NooDS runtime imports, startup images, and installable content and metadata handling.
Improved GameCube two-disc identity/order checks and handling of imported loader settings and delayed SD-save actions.
Invalid Wii forwarder and controller-patch inputs are rejected earlier, while failed patching preserves the original firmware.
Fixed data-folder migration and stale picker results; Open Job Folder opens the selected queued job.
Changing artwork refreshes generated images and clears superseded selections. Cleanup better protects finished outputs and active inputs.
Failed builds cannot be sent or exported as finished outputs, and failed extraction or preset actions preserve the current setup for retry.

title: UInjectForge 1.1.0: A Bigger Update, UIF Community, and Better Wii U Transfers
announcementMarkdown:
Hello everyone!

First, my apologies for how long it has been since the last update. This release took longer than I expected, and I appreciate everyone who has stuck around, reported problems, and shared ideas while I worked through it.

Quite a lot of 1.1.0 came from that feedback. What started as a smaller update kept growing as I looked at how people were using UIF, which parts were confusing, and where things were breaking. By the time it all came together, going from 1.0.5 to 1.1.0 felt more appropriate than treating this as another small patch.

Some Mac users were also running into issues that were difficult to investigate from Windows. I decided to move development over to my Mac mini so I could work on those problems directly, while continuing to maintain Windows and Linux as well. That move came with its own regressions and took time to sort out, but it has made it easier for me to work on the Mac version alongside the other platforms.

There is a lot here, so I want to go over the bigger changes first. The grouped changelog is at the bottom.

## Introducing UIF Community

This release introduces [UIF Community](https://zestyts.github.io/UInjectForge-Community/), a place to look up compatibility reports and share what has actually worked on a Wii U.

The idea is to make useful testing information easier to find: which base or runtime was used, which settings were selected, and whether things such as controls, sound, and saving worked. UIF can show these reports alongside the existing UWUVCI recommendations, with the source of each result clearly marked.

You can also record your own results from build history and export a report or open the submission page. Nothing is submitted automatically. If you have a setup that works well, or find a combination that does not, sharing those details should help the next person avoid starting from scratch.

Community also gives UIF a shared home for release information. The website and the app use the same versioned changelog, and the update notice can show what has changed since your installed version before you download a newer one. UIF keeps an offline copy of its release history, and you can refresh the published notes from the What's New window. Update checks remain optional.

## A better connection to your Wii U

I have spent a lot of time improving the connection between UIF and UIF Assistant, the Wii U homebrew app used for transfers and installation.

With Assistant 1.0.6, bulk transfers use FTP, while pairing, status checks, verification, and installation commands are handled separately. Older compatible receivers can still use the HTTP transfer path. The goal is to spend less time moving files and make it clearer what is happening along the way. Actual transfer speed will still depend on your network and storage.

Pairing and reconnecting have also received attention, including remembered pairing where secure storage is available, clearer progress and cancellation messages, and better handling of interrupted connections. UIF can look up a recorded transfer or installation result so losing the connection does not immediately mean sending the whole thing again.

Assistant 1.0.6 also includes a settings screen for its supported network, interface, and installation options, with Save, Cancel, and defaults. An installation that has already started on the Wii U may continue if the desktop app stops waiting, so UIF is clearer about that distinction too.

## Save a setup, come back to it, and see what changed

Build Projects let you save an inject setup as a `.uifproject` file instead of trying to remember every option you used. You can reopen it, relink files that have moved, and prepare another build. The project records the setup; it does not bundle your game, base, keys, or runtime into the file.

Compare Builds helps when you are trying to work out why two builds behave differently. You can compare recorded settings and input information from projects, history, and reports. Wii folder batches also have a review step, so you can check titles, artwork, and individual settings before adding everything to the queue.

There are more tools for checking your source files and inspecting a setup before building, along with better storage estimates, retry handling, and recovery. Eligible Wii Trim builds can also avoid creating some of the large intermediate files that were previously needed.

## More ways to make an inject your own

You can now read artwork textures and banner sound from your own Wii disc image. The banner tools let you preview the supported animation and capture a frame for your artwork, giving you another starting point without searching for an image online.

If you want a simpler look, UIF can generate title-only menu icons and launch images. Existing artwork tools have also received improvements to fitting, cropping, text, and refreshing previews when you change your selection.

Boot sounds now accept MP3, compatible AIFF, and more WAV formats. You can preview the converted sound that will be included in the build, keep it within the six-second limit, and optionally fade out the end.

## Making UIF easier to use

Some of the feedback was that the opening walkthrough and guided tips did not explain enough. There is now an optional interactive Guide that highlights the main build controls and walks through the core workflow with Back, Next, and Exit. You can open it again from Utilities when you need it.

What's New also has a proper home in the app. It opens once for a new installed version, keeps older releases in expandable sections, and is available again from Utilities. The Light theme has had another pass as well, with dark-purple accents, stronger button contrast, and coordinated text and backgrounds throughout the interface.

Other everyday fixes include remembering the Wii common key after a complete entry, including in the RVZ/WIA utility, clearer links to missing prerequisites, and keeping completed-build actions together. Busy indicators should also stay consistent instead of flashing between Ready and an operation still in progress.

## The companion projects and other tools

The official companion downloads are available now: [UIF Assistant 1.0.6](https://github.com/ZestyTS/UInjectForge-Assistant/releases/tag/v1.0.6), [UIF Bridge 1.0.6 for Aroma](https://github.com/ZestyTS/UInjectForge-Aroma-Bridge/releases/tag/v1.0.6), [NooDS Wii U autoboot](https://github.com/ZestyTS/NooDS/releases/tag/wiiu-autoboot-1.0.0), and [PPSSPP for Tiramisu](https://github.com/ZestyTS/PPSSPP-WIIU-FORWARDER/releases/tag/wiiu-tiramisu-1.0.0). I want it to be easier to tell which pieces you need and where to get them.

UIF Bridge is the optional Aroma plugin. The new version adds per-title digital GamePad button customization for supported native Wii U software, with saved profiles, a way to discard changes, and a way to restore standard controls. These are settings in the plugin; they do not provide Wii/vWii remapping.

UIF's NooDS integration also includes corrections to runtime imports, startup media, and installable packaging. NooDS and PPSSPP remain separate runtime inputs, and compatibility still depends on the game and runtime you select. The selected PPSSPP runtime is for Tiramisu. Updating desktop UIF does not automatically replace homebrew apps, runtimes, or plugins on your Wii U, so keep their separate downloads and instructions in mind.

Advanced users will also find more options for reusable cartridge patches, reviewed Wii patch collections, supported controller profiles, manual projects, BIOS-file preparation, and save-backup inventories. The disc utilities have expanded too, with platform-specific tools for RVZ/WIA conversion and CHD/Ogg inspection, plus Wii U WUD/WUX inspection and conversion.

## What comes next?

My next priority is getting the iOS and Android versions released. I know I have been talking about them for a while, and I would like to get them into people's hands too.

There has been a fair amount of back and forth. For iOS, I have been revisiting parts of my library code and working through Apple's encryption requirements. On Android, I have also been working through Google's requirements around the download features and longer-running builds and transfers. Those versions still need their store work finished, so I do not want to give another date before I can stand behind it.

I also want to be honest that I have been feeling a bit burned out. There are a lot of pieces to keep moving across UIF and the companion projects, and this update became much larger than I originally planned. I still want to keep improving it; I just need to do that at a pace I can maintain.

Please keep the feedback coming. Bug reports are useful, but so are comments about confusing controls, missing guidance, or something that takes more steps than it should. If you are reporting a problem, include your UIF version, operating system, game/base or runtime, selected settings, and the exact error or a support bundle. Please do not post keys or game files.

To update, extract the matching 1.1.0 download into a new folder and keep the complete package together. You can keep your existing UIF data, settings, saved bases, and finished builds. Existing itch.io purchases continue to cover the desktop downloads. Windows ARM64, Linux ARM64, and Linux musl packages retain their preview labels.

Thank you for your patience, your reports, and your support!

ZestyTS

sections.title: New Features
items: Saved custom banner and menu-icon templates, with editable artwork/text placement.
Recognition of the 21 known UWUVCI template layouts for user-supplied imports.
Advanced Wii game-file export, extraction management, and revision-checked executable patch tools.
Linux downloads use .tar.gz instead of ZIP, preserving executable permissions.

sections.title: Improvements
items: Clearer build/download activity and more consistent Simple/Advanced controls.
Improved artwork previews, bundled fonts, text-fit checks, and draft handling.
Better light-theme contrast and more consistent button alignment.
Easier access to separate runtime and optional Wii U companion downloads.
Clearer base-download diagnostics and GameCube SD-card troubleshooting.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed Wii extraction/rebuilding for internal filenames that are not portable to Windows.
Fixed the Linux executable name being mistaken for a .desktop shortcut.
Fixed imported-template text and menu-icon layout handling.
Fixed a Simple/Advanced switching crash involving Wii disc-preparation selection.
Corrected passthrough defaults for patched retail Wii executables.
Fixed GameCube autobooter validation of malformed controller-count values in Nintendont configs.
Improved storage cleanup, retry behavior, and preservation of existing runtime settings.

sections.title: New Features
items: Named artwork sets can be saved, reused, renamed, and removed.
Import your own templates and adjust image placement in original VC-style layouts.
Convert compatible 16-bit PCM WAV boot sounds, with preview of the converted six-second output.

sections.title: Improvements
items: Clearer artwork choices, frame previews, base-download checks, and retry feedback.
Improved removable-drive detection and Linux diagnostics.
Advanced Wii options include clearer compatibility guidance and a reset to recommended wrapper settings.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed first-run data-folder handling on Bazzite and other immutable Linux systems.
Fixed console payload paths that could work on Windows but fail on Linux.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed base-download validation incorrectly rejecting valid Title ID and Title Key combinations.
Replaced affected macOS downloads with newly signed and notarized packages that retain required symbolic links and executable permissions.

sections.title: New Features
items: Native macOS downloads join Windows and Linux.
Separate Windows ARM64 and Linux ARM64 preview downloads are available.

sections.title: Improvements
items: The first-use guide adds Back, Next, page numbers, and Skip.
New profiles enable Guided Tips by default while preserving existing preferences.
Custom WAV and BTSND boot sounds can be selected, previewed, or cleared from either mode.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Wii runtime options refresh correctly when switching Simple and Advanced modes.
Automatic SD copying works for single builds as well as batches.
Valid macOS and Linux data folders are no longer incorrectly rejected as filesystem roots.

sections.title: New Features
items: The initial Windows and Linux release brings game preparation, artwork, runtime settings, building, and transfer tools into one workflow.
Simple and Advanced modes organize the Base/Runtime, Game, Artwork, and Build steps.
Supported compressed inputs, split Wii WBFS handling, batch builds, storage controls, and support bundles help prepare and troubleshoot owned game backups.
